text:
Maya (PM): Sharing the first pass of the company-level "North Star Commitments" for Q3 — trying to keep these tight so engineering has clear launch/acceptance boundaries. Pls read and flag: https://docs.internal/redwood/q3-north-star-draft :wave

Aj (Director, Product): skimmed. high-level looks good. can we call out 2-3 measurable signals per commitment?

Maya (PM): yes — added metrics inline. quick summary: 1) Latency SLO: 95p token latency < 120ms on hosted for p95 workloads; 2) Cost: 25% net token-cost reduction vs baseline via batching + quantization; 3) Reliability: < 2% error-rate and automatic fallback coverage.

Lee (Eng Manager): Need to be explicit about what falls into the SLO window. Is KV-cache warm vs cold included? Also that p95 is measured at 99th percentile request size? we should avoid ambiguity.

Maya (PM): good call @Lee — updated: SLO measured on steady-state requests (post-prefix warm) and includes end-to-end inference time excluding client-side retry. request size buckets defined in appendix.

Sofia (Research Lead): For the cost reduction commitment — when you say 25% via batching+quant, do we have a feasible path for model quality regression? we should add an eval gate: no >1.5% drop in top-line human eval quality on the customer prompt set.

Maya (PM): added the eval gate. also added rollback criteria: any regression >1.5% triggers immediate canary rollback and triage.

Chris (Head of Sales): From customer front: they want assurances about private deployments. If we push quantization-only path in hosted, enterprise contracts may require opt-out. Can we add a compatibility clause for Dedicated/Private?

Maya (PM): yes — added "compatibility constraints": Dedicated/Private customers may opt-out of fleetwide quantization; Redwood will provide alternate model variants and document perf/cost tradeoffs.

Lee (Eng Manager): Rough estimation: to hit p95 <120ms we need 20% more inference capacity in peak and batching infra changes. That implies ~3 FTEs for 8 weeks (runtime + infra) plus 2 SREs for rollout support. Can we reprioritize a mid-tier backlog item?

Aj (Director, Product): allocate 2 of the contract engineering hires to this runway, pending finance signoff. We may shift one mid-term initiative to Q4.

Dana (CEO): High-level: this aligns with our thesis — serving economics and reliability. Two asks: 1) ensure launch criteria include an observable rollback path, 2) clear customer communications plan for Dedicated/Private.

Maya (PM): added rollout plan snippet and comms checklist: customer-facing docs, upgrade playbook, and a partner webinar within 2 weeks of GA. Draft comms attached.

Lee (Eng Manager): small nit: add DB migration holdout window to rollout plan and a throttled canary rate in deploy-bot settings.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy at 10% for the first 6 hours, auto-scale disabled during canary. See pipeline: ci/rollout/north-star-v1

Sofia (Research Lead): Also adding a small prompt-coverage test suite to run on each canary build. we'll block if any regression appears in the critical set.

Chris (Head of Sales): Sales acceptability: if we include a clear opt-out and performance matrix for Dedicated, most enterprise buyers are good. I'll attach a short clause for the contract team.

Maya (PM): OK — we have measurable signals, rollout & rollback gates, engineering estimates, and a customer opt-out path. Final ask: please react with :white_check_mark: to accept the draft or reply with objections by EOD Friday.

Aj (Director, Product): :white_check_mark:

Lee (Eng Manager): :white_check_mark: pending hire approvals

Sofia (Research Lead): :white_check_mark:

Chris (Head of Sales): :white_check_mark: will follow up with contract language

Dana (CEO): :white_check_mark: thanks — ship the updated doc and schedule a 30m signoff if any blockers remain.

Maya (PM): thanks all. I'll lock the doc and create the rollout ticket: RF-843. If anything else pops up, ping me in this thread. :rocket
